Blake Huber

Libertarian candidate for United States Senator, Colorado · Challenger

Property and business manager; election-reform activist

Blake Huber is the Libertarian Party nominee for U.S. Senate in Colorado on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot. He has worked in management for more than 30 years and has served as a state chair of the Libertarian Party and as a member of its national committee. Before this race he ran on the Approval Voting Party ticket for Vice President (2016), Colorado Secretary of State (2018), and President (2020 and 2024).

Where Huber stands

Election reform / Voting methods
Supports approval voting, which he also calls satisfaction voting. Under it, voters can back more than one candidate. He says this would produce results that better reflect what voters want and help find middle ground.
Legal immigration
Supports immigration reform that, in his words, makes it easier for good people to contribute.
Regulation / Small business
Supports regulation reform that reduces what he calls unnecessary burdens on small businesses.

Background

  • Libertarian nominee for U.S. Senate, Colorado (2026)
  • Approval Voting Party candidate for President of the United States (2020, 2024)
  • Approval Voting Party candidate for Colorado Secretary of State (2018)
  • Approval Voting Party candidate for Vice President of the United States (2016)
  • Former state chair of the Libertarian Party and former member of its national committee
  • More than 30 years in management: apartment communities, a small business, a motel, and network engineering teams
  • Military service listed by BallotReady: Kansas National Guard; U.S. Navy Reserve
